places.title: Campus Martius
places.description: The Campus Martius or "field of Mars" is the name given to the level ground between the slopes of the Capitoline, the Quirinal, and Pincian hills, and the Tiber river.

places.title: Monteverde
places.description: The hill of Monteverde, a part of the Ianiculum hill to the west of the Tiber river, was a source of a brown, lithoid tuff (tufo di Monteverde) that was quarried for use as a building material from the second century BC.

places.title: Naumachia
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 Naumachia

places.title: Pietra Papa
places.description: In terms of modern toponymy, Pietra Papa describes a place on the right bank of the Tiber River where today a riverside avenue (Lungotevere di Pietra Papa) links the Lungotevere Vittorio Gassman to Piazza Augusto Righi. Palmer asserts that the toponym "Pietra Papa" dates to the Middle Ages. Excavati

places.title: Roma
places.description: The capital of the Roman Republic and Empire.

places.title: S. Felicita
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 S. Felicita

places.title: S. Ippolito
places.description: A catacomb connected with the Christian Saint Hippolytus of Rome along the Via Tiburtina.

locations.title: Imagery location of Catacomba di Sant'Ippolito

places.title: S. Laurentius
places.description: The Papal Basilica of Saint Lawrence outside the Walls (Basilica Papale di San Lorenzo fuori le Mura) is one of the Seven Pilgrim Churches of Rome. The basilica serves as the shrine and tomb dedicated to Saint Lawrence and its earliest phases likely belong to the fourth century AD.

locations.title: OSM location of Basilica of Saint Lawrence outside the Walls

places.title: S. Petrus
names: Basilica Papale di San Pietro in Vaticano
places.description: The Basilica of St. Peter in Vatican City is currently a Renaissance edifice standing on the site of Old St. Peter's Basilica, a church built by Constantine I between 319 and 333 CE. The holy site is located on the Mons Vaticanus in connection with the purported site of the burial of the Christian S

locations.title: OSM location of Saint Peter's Basilica

places.title: Sep. Geta
places.description: A Roman tomb along the Via Appia that is traditionally believed to be that of Publius Septimius Geta, the younger son of Septimius Severus.

locations.title: OSM location of Sepolcro di Geta

places.title: Villa Esmeade
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 Villa Esmeade

places.title: Villa Pamphili
places.description: The church of San Pancrazio was founded in the sixth century A.D. by Pope Symmachus. It stands beyond the Porta San Pancrazio on the Ianiculum. Below the church is a massive catacomb referred to as S. Pancrazio or Ottavilla.

locations.title: OSM location of Basilica di San Pancrazio

places.title: Villa Torlonia
places.description: A Jewish catacomb discovered in 1919 on the grounds of the Villa Torlonia park in Rome.

places.title: Aqua Anio Vetus
places.description: Aqua Anio Vetus, an aqueduct serving Rome and built originally during the third century BC. The Anio Vetus carried water to Rome from the Aniene near Vicovaro.

places.title: Aqua Antoniniana
places.description: The Aqua Antoniniana was a branch of the Aqua Marcia that carried water to the Baths of Caracalla.

places.title: Aqua Appia
places.description: The earliest of Rome's aqueducts, the Aqua Appia was constructed in 312 BC by the censor Appius Claudius Caecus. The aqueduct runs a course of 16.4 km, entering Rome at the Porta Maggiore. Frontinus estimated the daily volume at 75,537 cubic meters.

locations.title: Imagery Location: aqueduct segment at Piazza Celimontana

places.title: Aqua Traiana
places.description: The Aqua Traiana was an aqueduct built by Trajan and inaugurated in AD 109.

places.title: Aqua Virgo
places.description: The Aqua Virgo was one of the 11 aqueducts supplying the city of Rome and was completed by Marcus Agrippa in 19 BC. The aqueduct was later revitalized by Pope Adrian I in the eighth century.

places.title: Pons Aemilius
places.description: The Pons Aemilius was the first stone bridge built across the Tiber River at Rome (241 B.C.). Its remains are known today as the 'Ponte Rotto'.

places.title: Unnamed bridge in the Piazza Eugenio Biffi
names: Unnamed bridge in the Piazza Eugenio Biffi
places.description: The remains of an ancient Roman bridge in the present Piazza Eugenio Biffi in Rome. This bridge is thought to have spanned the Almo river.

places.title: Untitled
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 no. 11 (bridge near so-called Tomb of Geta)

places.title: Cemetery of Gordianus, Epimachus, Apronianus
names: Catacomb of Saints Gordian and Epimachus
places.description: A burial ground for the the Christian martyrs Gordianus, Epimachus, and Apronianus at the seventh mile of the Via Latina.

locations.title: Imagery location of Catacomb of Saints Gordian and Epimachus

places.title: Ad Malum Punicum
places.description: Ad Malum Punicum describes a street on the Alta Semita in ancient Rome, likely corresponding to the modern Via delle Quattro Fontane. Vespasian owned a domus in this street and it was here that the future emperor Domitian was born.

locations.title: OSM location of Via delle Quattro Fontane

places.title: ad Capita bubula
places.description: The toponym "ad Capita bubula" is attested in Suetonius and refers to a place located at the northeast corner of the Palatine Hill in Rome near the Curiae Veteres. Here, there was a domus of one Caius Octavius, a Roman politician who was the biological father of Octavian. It is possible that Octavia

places.title: Porta Capena
places.description: The Porta Capena was a gate in Rome's Republican city walls ("Servian Wall") located on the south-west slope of the Caelian Hill.

places.title: Arch of Gallienus
places.description: The Arch of Gallienus marked the Porta Esquilina, a gate in the Servian Wall of Rome. The via Labicana and via Tiburtina issue from Rome at this point. The arch was erected in A.D. 262.

locations.title: OSM location of Arch of Gallienus

places.title: Porta Naevia
places.description: The now-lost Porta Naevia was a minor gate in the Republican-period wall of the city of Rome. It was located on the Little Aventine and its position may correspond to the modern Largo Enzo Fioritto.

places.title: Arch of Titus (Circus Maximus)
places.description: A triple-bay triumphal arch was erected at the eastern end of the Circus Maximus in honor of Emperor Titus' role in the victory in the Jewish War. The arch is known from architectural and sculptural fragments and from an inscription recorded in the Einsiedeln sylloge.

locations.title: Imagery location of Arch of Titus (Circus Maximus)

places.title: Forum Augusti
places.description: The Forum of Augustus at Rome was dedicated in 2 BCE, to the northeast of Julius Caesar's Forum. It contained the Temple of Mars Ultor.

locations.title: OSM location of Forum of Augustus

places.title: Domus Clementis
places.description: The remains of a private domus that date to the second and third centuries CE and include a Mithraeum. This complex eventually became incorporated into the fourth-century basilica on the site of the later basilica of San Clemente al Laterano.

places.title: Tomb of Priscilla
places.description: A Roman tomb along the Via Appia that belonged to one Priscilla, wife of Titus Flavius Abascanto, a freedman of the emperor Domitian.

locations.title: OSM location of Tomb of Priscilla

places.title: Porticus Aemilia
places.description: A utilitarian porticus and storage building located outside the Porta Trigemina, the Porticus Aemilia was erected in 193 BCE by Marcus Aemilius Lepidus and and Lucius Aemilius Paullus.

places.title: Meta Romuli
places.description: The so-called "Meta Romuli" was a pyramidal tomb located in the Ager Vaticanus in Rome. It likely dates to the first century BCE or the first century CE. Its extant superstructure was demolished in 1499. Remains of foundations and pavements that have been associated with the tomb were encountered in

places.title: Porta Fontinalis
places.description: No longer extant, the Porta Fontinalis is only known via textual and epigraphic references. Presumed to be a gate of the Servian Wall, the Porta Fontinalis lay in the Campus Martius, west of the via Lata. It may have been the original point of issuance for the Republican roads known as the Via Flami

places.title: Temple of Vesta at Rome
places.description: The Temple of Vesta, located at the east end of the Forum Romanum.

locations.title: Imagery Location of the Temple of Vesta
OSM location of Temple of Vesta

places.title: Sette Sale
places.description: Cisterns of the imperial period on the Oppian Hill that once supplied the Baths of Trajan.

locations.title: OSM location of Cisterna delle Sette Sale

places.title: Pons Fabricius
places.description: The Pons Fabricius (sometimes referred to as the Ponte dei Quattro Capi) is a first-century BC bridge in Rome that spans part of the Tiber River from the area of the Circus Flaminius to the Tiber Island.

places.title: Circus Varianus
places.description: A circus that was part of the Sessorium palace next to the Amphitheatrum Castrense. The obelisk currently situated on the Pincian Hill was discovered on the site in the sixteenth century. It had been moved to the spina of the circus during the reign of Elagabalus.

places.title: Forum Holitorium
places.description: The Forum Holitorium was the vegetable market of ancient Rome, situated outside the Porta Carmentalis in the southern Campus Martius. This area was bounded by the Forum Boarium and the Circus Flaminius.

places.title: Oppius Mons
places.description: The Oppian Hill is the southern spur of Rome's Esquiline Hill.

locations.title: Imagery location of the Oppian Hill

places.title: Divorum
places.description: A porticus constructed by Domitian in A.D. 80 on the eastern Campus Martius on the site of the Villa Publica, whose northern entry—a triumphal arch—was flanked by two small temples in honor of Titus and Vespasian.

places.title: Pons Neronianus
places.description: A bridge across the Tiber river built either by Caius or Nero in order to connect the western part of the Campus Martius with the Campus Vaticanus.

places.title: Sacred Area of S. Omobono
places.description: An archaeological area in the Forum Boarium comprising an ancient ritual precinct with twin temples ranging in date from the Archaic period through the time of the Roman Empire. The Medieval church dedicated to S. Omobono stands atop the remains of one of the two ancient temples.

locations.title: OSM Location of Sacred Area of S. Omobono
OSM location of Temples of the Sacred Area of S. Ombono

places.title: Murus Servii Tullii
places.description: The Republican city wall of Rome.

places.title: Vaticanus Ager
places.description: A district on the right bank of the river Tiber, between the lower course of the river and the territory of Veii.

places.title: via Taranto columbaria
places.description: Two Roman columbaria are located under the present via Pescara, 2. This accounts for the tomb being referred to interchangeably with two modern, street-derived toponyms, namely "via Taranto" and "via Pescara". These tombs are situated near the ancient crossroads of the via Latina and the via Labican

locations.title: OSM location of Colombari di via Taranto

places.title: Quirinal Hill
places.description: One of the hills of Rome comprises several smaller peaks. According to tradition, its first inhabitants were Titus Tatius and the Sabines; during the Republic, the hill was mostly residential.

places.title: Pantheon
places.description: A temple in the Campus Martius of Rome that was first built by Marcus Agrippa (ca. 27-25 B.C.) and then rebuilt by the emperor Hadrian (after A.D. 126). In A.D. 609, the structure was consecrated as a Christian church, S. Maria ad Martyres.

places.title: Palatine Stadium
places.description: "Palatine Stadium" is likely a misnomer when considering the probable function of this architectural complex located on the southeast corner of the Palatine Hill on the flank of the Domus Augustana-Flavia. Originating during the reign of the Domitian, this complex was restored numerous times, includ

places.title: Templum Pacis
places.description: The Temple of Peace in Rome was vowed by Vespasian following the Jewish War.

places.title: Clivus Capitolinus
places.description: The principal road leading to the Capitolium and the Arx in the city of Rome.

places.title: Paedagogium
places.description: The so-called Pedagogium is a building that was part of the Flavian palace complex on the Palatine Hill. It was located below the exedra of the façade of the Domus Augustana. The Paedagogium is thought to have superseded the late-Republican domus known as the Domus Gelotiana.

places.title: Temple of Castor and Pollux (Rome)
places.description: Located at the southeast corner of the Forum Romanum, the aedes Castoris is a temple of ancient Rome vowed by the dictator Postumius in 499 BCE.

locations.title: OSM location of Temple of Castor and Pollux

places.title: Velia
places.description: The Velia, no longer extant, was a spur stretching from the north side of the Palatine Hill toward the Oppian Hill.

places.title: Circus Flaminius
places.description: Located in the southern Campus Martius, the Circus Flaminius is a large area built by C. Flaminius Nepos in 221 B.C. Various games, including the ludi plebeii, ludi Taurii, ludi saeculares, were celebrated here. The circus was also a place of popular assembly.

places.title: Domus Romane di Palazzo Valentini
places.description: The remains of a Roman domus and a bath complex adjacent to the area of the Forum of Trajan.

locations.title: OSM location of Domus Romane di Palazzo Valentini

places.title: Arcus Dolabellae et Silani
places.description: Situated on the Caelian Hill, the Arcus Dolabellae et Silani sits at the northern corner of the Castra Peregrina. The gate dates to A.D. 10 and is likely a rebuilding of an earlier gate that was part of the so-called Servian Wall, perhaps the Porta Querquetulana (or Querquetularia) or the Porta Cael

places.title: Porticus Pompei
places.description: A porticus built in 55 B.C. in connection with the Theater of Pompey. The Curia Pompei, site of Iulius Caesar's assassination in 44 B.C., was likely located within the portico.

places.title: Horti Sallustiani
places.description: The gardens of Sallust in Regio VI of the ancient city of Rome.

places.title: Basilica Julia
places.description: The Basilica Julia was built on the south side of the Forum Romanum in 46 B.C. on the site of the former Basilica Sempronia.

places.title: tribus Menenia
places.description: The gens Menenia was an ancient patrician line that lent its name to the tribus Menenia.

places.title: So-called Arco di Druso
places.description: The popular toponym associated with this monument - Arco di Druso or Arch of Drusus - is a misnomer and is misleading. This is problematic given other textual, epigraphic, and archaeological attestations that mention honorific monuments dedicated to Nero Claudius Drusus. This place is the site of th

locations.title: OSM location of Arch of Drusus

places.title: Thermae Traiani
places.description: A monumental public bath of ancient Rome that was built between 104 and 109. The architect Apollodorus of Damascus built the baths for Trajan.

locations.title: OSM location of Baths of Trajan

places.title: Temple of Magna Mater
places.description: The Temple of Magna Mater, also known as the Temple of Cybele, was dedicated near the Clivus Victoriae on the Palatine Hill on 11 April 191 BCE. The original temple was destroyed by fire in 111 BCE. Following another series of destructive fires, Augustus restored the temple, as he records in his Res

locations.title: OSM location of Tempio di Magna Mater

places.title: Temple of Vespasian and Titus
places.description: A temple in the Roman Forum dedicated to the deified Vespasian that was begun by Titus and completed under Domitian.

locations.title: OSM location of Temple of Vespasian and Titus

places.title: Capitolium Vetus
places.description: The Capitolium Vetus was located on the Quirinal Hill and was an earlier shrine to the triad of Iuppiter, Juno, and Minerva than the famous Capitoline Temple. It was likely perched on the northern edge of the Quirinal.

places.title: Pyramid of Cestius
places.description: An ancient pyramid-shaped tomb built for Caius Cestius (ca. 18-12 BC), a magistrate and member of the Septemviri Epulonum. The tomb stands at the fork of the ancient Via Ostiensis and was later incorporated into the city's fortifications.

locations.title: Imagery location of the Pyramid of Cestius
OSM location of Pyramid of Cestius

places.title: Torre Dell'Angelo
places.description: A Roman columbarium tomb located on the Via Latina.

locations.title: OSM location of Sepolcro In Laterizio II Secolo d.c. Detto Torre Dell' Angelo

places.title: Forum Boarium (at Rome)
places.description: Rome's so-called "cattle market", the Forum Boarium is a key area of commercial and ritual activity on the east bank of the river Tiber. It is flanked by the Capitoline, Palatine, and Aventine hills.

places.title: Ara Maxima Herculis
places.description: An early cult center connected with Herakles located in Rome's Forum Boarium.

places.title: Pons Cestius
places.description: A Roman stone bridge on the Tiber River, spanning the river channel from the Tiber Island westward to the Transtiberim (Trastevere). The original bridge dates to the first century BC.

places.title: Sep. Eurysacis
places.description: The tomb of a baker, M. Vergilius Eurysaces, built at the point where the via Labicana and the via Praenestina exit from Rome's walls to the east. The tomb dates to the later Republican period (ca. 50-20 B.C.).

locations.title: OSM location of Sepolcro del fornaio Eurisace

places.title: Porticus Octaviae
places.description: A porticus in the area of the Circus Flaminius, the Porticus Octaviae was dedicated by Augustus sometime after 27 B.C. in honor of his sister, Octavia Minor. The porticus replaced the Porticus Metelli. It was restored twice after major urban fires in A.D. 80 and 203.

places.title: Arch of Titus
places.description: A triumphal arch erected in summa Sacra Via and dedicated to the deified emperor Titus by his brother Domitian, ca. 81 CE.

locations.title: OSM location of Arch of Titus

places.title: Temple of Veiovis
places.description: The Temple of Veiovis, also attested as Aedes Vediovis, was a temple of ancient Rome located on the Capitoline Hill in a location known as "inter duos lucos", which is interpreted to mean a saddle between the two summits of the hill. The remains of a temple podium were discovered beneath the northwe

locations.title: Imagery location of Temple of Veiovis

places.title: Porticus Absidata
places.description: The Porticus Absidata was an exedra porticata that served as the northern apsidal entryway to the Forum of Nerva, also known as the Forum Transitorium.

places.title: Forum Traiani
places.description: Imperial forum constructed at Rome under Trajan between 105-112 CE.

locations.title: OSM location of Foro di Traiano

places.title: House of Augustus
places.description: An elite domus located at the southwest corner of the Palatine Hill that is identified as the house lived in by the Roman emperor Augustus.

locations.title: OSM location of Casa di Augusto

places.title: Tugurium Romuli
places.description: Ancient textual sources, including Dionysius of Halicarnassus and Plutarch, place the purported dwelling place of Romulus near the Scalae Caci at the southwestern corner of the Palatine Hill in Rome. Whether the place cited by ancient texts and maintained in antiquity until at least the fourth centu

places.title: Privata domus Traiani
places.description: The so-called "Privata domus Traiani" was an opulent townhouse on the Aventine Hill in Rome. Its foundations were eventually coopted in the third century CE for the construction of the Baths of Decius. Evidence from brickstamps dates the building to the Trajanic to early Antonine period, leading som

locations.title: OSM location of Privata Traiani Domus

places.title: Aedes Apollinis Palatini
places.description: The temple sacred to the god Apollo on the Palatine Hill in Rome.

locations.title: OSM location of Tempio di Apollo

places.title: Templum Veneris et Romae
places.description: A double temple sacred to Venus Felix and Roma Aeterna built by Hadrian on the slope of the Velian hill to the north of the Sacra Via beginning in 121 CE.

locations.title: OSM location of Tempio di Venere e Roma

places.title: Clivus Scauri
places.description: A street that ascended from the depression between the Palatine and the Caelian hills.

locations.title: OSM location of Clivo di Scauro

places.title: Porta Collina
places.description: The Porta Collina was a gate in Rome's Servian Wall located on the Quirinal Hill. At the Porta Collina the Via Salaria and the Via Nomentana divided. Some remains of the gate were identified in 1872 on the Via Venti Settembre beneath the Italian Ministry of Finance.

places.title: Praedia Galbana
places.description: A tract of suburban land located southwest of the Aventine Hill that would come to be the location of the Horrea Galbae.

places.title: Temple of Divus Iulius
places.description: The temple on the Sacra Via dedicated to the deified Iulius Caesar, authorized in 42 B.C. and built by Augustus, with its dedication occurring on 18th August, 29 B.C.

locations.title: OSM location of Temple of Divus Iulius

places.title: Mausoleum Augusti
places.description: A monumental tomb built in the Campus Martius at Rome by Augustus and dedicated in 28 B.C. The mausoleum served as a family tomb for the Iulio-Claudians.

locations.title: OSM location of Mausoleum of Augustus

places.title: Amphitheatrum Flavium
places.description: The Flavian amphitheater at Rome (the so-called "Colosseum").

places.title: Domus di Vigna Guidi
places.description: A well-appointed domus of the mid-second century CE that was consumed by the construction works to create the Thermae Antoninianae, resulting in its being buried to a depth of some 10 m in construction fill. Heritage officials describe the house as a sort of 'condominium', comparing it to the contem

locations.title: OSM location of Domus di Vigna Guidi

places.title: Theatrum Marcelli
places.description: Theatrum Marcelli (Theater of Marcellus) is an ancient Roman theater in the Circus Flaminius. Augustus completed its construction and dedicated it in 12 BC.

locations.title: OSM Location of Visible Remains of Theater
OSM location of Area archeologica del Teatro di Marcello

places.title: Porta Trigemina
places.description: Now lost, the Porta Trigemina was one of the main gates of the Servian Wall.

places.title: Tomba della Medusa (Roma)
places.description: A Roman chamber tomb now located on the grounds of the Policlinico Umberto I hospital in Rome.

locations.title: Imagery Location of Tomba della Medusa

places.title: Arcus Tiberii
places.description: A single-bay triumphal arch dedicated to Tiberius in 16 CE. This arch commemorated the recovery of Varus' standards lost in 9 CE. It stood on the Sacra Via at the northwest corner of the Basilica Iulia.

locations.title: Imagery location of Arch of Tiberius

places.title: Thermae Antoninianae
places.description: The Thermae Antoninianae, commonly known as the Baths of Caracalla, were built in Rome between AD 212 and 216.

locations.title: OSM location of Baths of Caracalla

places.title: Lapis Niger
places.description: A shrine in the Forum Romanum adjacent to the Republican comitium, recognizable by the distinctive black paving stones that covered it in the later republican period. The shrine has been associated, in tradition, with the tomb of Romulus and/or of Faustulus. Giacomo Boni excavated the site between 1

places.title: Pons Aelius
places.description: The Pons Aelius or Aelian Bridge (now Ponte Sant'Angelo) was completed by Hadrian in AD 134 to span the Tiber opposite the new mausoleum of the emperor.

places.title: Arcus Argentariorum
places.description: A commemorative arch located in the Velabrum dedicated to the Severan emperors in AD 204 by the local association of money-changers (argentarii) and merchants (negotiantes). It was later incorporated into the church of S. Giorgio al Velabro.

places.title: Porticus Philippi
places.description: A portico that surrounded the Temple of Hercules Musarum in the Campus Martius of ancient Rome. The construction of the portico was the result of the patronage of L. Marcius Philippus, the stepfather of Augustus.

places.title: Capitolinus Mons
places.description: The smallest of Rome's hills and one of its most important, the Capitoline Hill served as the citadel (arx) of the city and as the site of its poliadic temple.

places.title: Porta Querquetulana
places.description: The Porta Querquetulana was a gateway of Rome's so-called Servian Walls. It derived its name from from a sacred grove of oaks that seems to have vanished by the first century BCE.

places.title: Temple of Jupiter Tonans
places.description: A small temple to Jupiter the Thunderer, most likely located in the Area Capitolina. Vowed by Augustus in 26 BCE and dedicated in 22 BCE.

places.title: Porta Rauduscula
places.description: The Porta Rauduscula was a gate of Rome's so-called Servian Wall. It is known only from textual sources. Varro's listing places it between the Porta Naevia and the Porta Lavernalis.

places.title: Aedes Herculis Pompeiani
places.description: A temple of Hercules located near the Circus Maximus.

places.title: Tomb of Quintus Sulpicius Maximus
places.description: The tomb of the boy poet Quintus Sulpicius Maximus on the Via Salaria in Rome. He died in 94 CE, aged just 11 years.

locations.title: OSM location of Sepolcro del Giovinetto Quinto Sulpicio Massimo

places.title: Basilica Neptuni
places.description: A building in the Campus Martius that originally dates to ca. 25 BCE.

places.title: Hypogeum of the Aurelii
places.description: A third-century AD hypogeum tomb on the Esquiline Hill in Rome with both pagan and Paleochristian iconography.

locations.title: Imagery location of Hypogeum of the Aurelii

places.title: domus Gelotiana
places.description: A domus on the slope of the Palatine Hill that Caius incorporated into the Imperial Palace complex.

places.title: Arch of Septimius Severus
places.description: The Arch of Septimius Severus is situated at the northwest corner of the Forum Romanum. It was dedicated in A.D. 203 and serves to commemorate the Parthian victories of Emperor Septimius Severus and his two sons against the Parthians (194/195 and 197–199).

locations.title: OSM location of Arch of Septimius Severus

places.title: Monte Testaccio
places.description: An artificial mountain on the banks of the Tiber River at Rome composed of 580,000 cubic meters of broken amphorae.

places.title: Horti Maiani
places.description: An urban garden of imperial Rome located on the summit of the Esquiline Hill. Based on an inscription dating to the reign of Claudius, it is believed that these gardens were administered by the same magistrate in charge of the Horti Lamiani, an official with the title "procurator hortorum Maianorum

places.title: Aedes Salus
places.description: While consul in 311 BCE, Caius Iunius Bubulcus Brutus vowed the temple of Salus; he would later dedicate it as dictator in 302 BCE. While no physical remains of the temple are known, textual and epigraphic testimony suggest that it would have been located near the present-day Piazza del Quirinale.

places.title: Colonnacce
places.description: Le Colonnacce refers to preserved elements of the lateral, north-south Corinthian-order colonnades that flanked the Forum Transitorium.

places.title: Columbarium of Pomponius Hylas
places.description: A Roman columbarium on the Via Appia close to the Porta Latina. The columbarium was excavated in 1831 by Pietro Campana.

locations.title: OSM location of Colombario di Pomponio Hylas

places.title: Circus Gaii et Neronis
places.description: Circus Gaii et Neronis was originally built as a private racecourse for the emperor Caius. In the fourth century A.D., the north side of the circus was destroyed in order to make room for the first basilica of St. Peter.

locations.title: OSM location of Circus Gai et Neronis

places.title: Basilica Argentaria
places.description: The toponym "Basilica Argentaria" is a descriptor that appears in fourth-century CE sources for a porticoed complex that dates to the reign of Trajan. This complex was built between the slope of the Capitoline Hill and the Forum Iulium during the terraforming of the Quirinal Hill that created space

places.title: Mausoleum of Lucilius Peto
places.description: A tumulus-type tomb discovered in 1887 belonging to the military tribune M. Lucilius Paetus of the gens Lucilia.

locations.title: Imagery location of the mausoleum of Lucilius Peto
OSM location of Mausoleo di Lucilio Peto

places.title: Nymphaeum divi Alexandri
places.description: A monumental nymphaeum on the Esquiline Hill dating to the Severan period; commonly known as "Trofei di Mario". The complex is located at a fork between the Via Tiburtina and the Via Labicana.

locations.title: OSM location of Ninfeo di Alessandro Severo

places.title: Theater of Nero
places.description: The Theater of Nero, located in the Vaticanus Ager, is relatively little known and receives little attention in the ancient sources. Archaeological discoveries announced in the summer of 2023 seem to point to remains of the theater preserved beneath the courtyard of the Palazzo della Rovere, located

locations.title: OSM location of Theatre of Nero

places.title: Domus Aurea
places.description: A sprawling palace complex begun by Nero after A.D. 64 that aimed to connect the Esquiline, Caelian, and Palatine hills.

locations.title: OSM location of Esquiline wing of the Domus Aurea

places.title: Basilica Aemilia
places.description: A basilica located at the juncture of the Sacra Via and the Argiletum flanking the Forum Romanum that was initially built in 179 B.C.E.

places.title: Horti Lucull(i)ani
places.description: An elite villa and garden on the Pincian Hill in Rome laid out originally by Lucius Licinius Lucullus ca. 60 BC. The present day Villa Borghese gardens still cover a portion of the Gardens of Lucullus.

places.title: Meta Sudans
places.description: A large fountain located southwest of the Flavian Amphitheater and completed under Domitian (ca. A.D. 96). Four of Rome's Augustan regions converged at this point (I, III, IV, X); it is possible that Regio II also intersected the other four regiones at this place.

places.title: Nymphaeum of via degli Annibaldi
places.description: An elaborate nymphaeum on the Oppian Hill discovered in 1895. The complex dates to the Late Republican period. The ancient nymphaeum was partially obliterated by the construction of the Neronian Domus Aurea.

locations.title: Imagery location of Nymphaeum of the via degli Annibaldi

places.title: Thermae Diocletiani
places.description: Public baths near the Viminal Hill in Rome constructed under Diocletian from 298-306 CE.

locations.title: OSM location of Terme di Diocleziano

places.title: Janiculum
places.description: This hill is located outside the ancient city of Rome, to the west of the Tiber River, and is not considered one of the Seven Hills of Rome. From an early stage, the Janiculum was connected to the city by fortifications and a bridge over the Tiber. It was also the site of important water-powered mil

places.title: Lucus Furrinae
places.description: The Lucus Furrinae or Syrian Sanctuary is a sanctuary site on the Janiculum Hill in Rome. The first known construction at the site took place during the late first century CE, and it remained in use until the mid-fourth century CE.

locations.title: OSM location of Santuario siriaco al Gianicolo
OSM location of Santuario siriaco al Gianicolo

places.title: Velabrum
places.description: The Velabrum is a valley in Rome that connects the Forum Romanum to the Forum Boarium.

places.title: Sacra Via
places.description: The Sacra Via (Sacred Way) is one of Rome's oldest urban streets and its main sacred route, extending from the top of the Velia (summa Sacra Via) to the Forum Romanum.

places.title: Temple of Divus Augustus (Rome)
places.description: Caius dedicated a temple to divus Augustus in Rome in the autumn of 37 CE. Based on the sources, the temple should be located between the vicus Tuscus and the vicus Iugarius, just behind the Basilica Iulia. The temple remains unexcavated, and its nature and location are a matter of scholarly debate.

places.title: Case Romane del Celio
places.description: An archaeological area beneath the basilica of the martyrs John and Paul that has been explored by means of excavation, revealing a series of Imperial period domestic remains dating between the second and fourth centuries A.D.

locations.title: OSM location of Case romane del Celio

places.title: Forum Iulium
places.description: The Forum Iulium (or Forum of Caesar, Forum Caesaris) is a forum built by Iulius Caesar and dedicated ca. 46 B.C. The main cult of the forum is that of Venus Genetrix.

locations.title: OSM location of Forum of Caesar

places.title: Arco di San Lazzaro
places.description: The so-called Arch of Saint Lazarus is part of a ruined arcuated structure located in Rome along Via Marmorata. Since this is the general vicinity of the ancient Emporium, these remains may belong to an ancient horreum. Medieval folklore associated the building with Horatius Cocles.

locations.title: OSM location of Arco di San Lazzaro (Roma)

places.title: Argiletum
places.description: The Argiletum was a street of ancient Rome that passed from the Forum Romanum and crossed the Suburra. Its route more or less followed that of the modern streets Via Leonina and Via della Madonna dei Monti.

places.title: Subura
places.description: Subura (or Suburra) refers to an area of ancient Rome, although the precise spatial definition of this area is unclear. In the earliest instances, this toponym may refer to the valley lying between the Oppian and the Caelian. As such it corresponds to one of the four urban regions known as the "Serv

places.title: Aedes Fauni
places.description: A temple dedicated to Faunus located on Tiber Island, the Aedes Fauni was dedicated in 196 BCE by Gnaeus Domitius Ahenobarbus and Gaius Scribonius Libo.

places.title: Circus Maximus
places.description: An ancient chariot-racing venue at Rome and a major location for public entertainments (ludi), the Circus Maximus is located between the Aventine and Palatine hills.

places.title: Lacus Curtius
places.description: The Lacus Curtius is an area in medio foro connected with the earliest phases of Rome's occupation. By the late Republican period, it had become a small basin set inside a paved area. Livy relates the famous episode of the Sabine Mettius Curtius in relation to his description of the site.

places.title: Palazzo Barberini Mithraeum
places.description: The Palazzo Barberini Mithraeum numbers among the best-preserved mithraic shrines in Rome. It is situated in via delle Quattro Fontane. Construction work revealed the site in 1936. A portion of the original structures of the second century CE was transformed into the mithraeum in the third century.

places.title: The Temple of Janus (Rome)
places.description: The now destroyed Temple of Janus near the Forum Romanum, Rome, was originally built in the reign of Numa, according to Livy.

places.title: Horrea Agrippiana
places.description: A set of warehouses in Regio VIII.

places.title: tribus Pollia
places.description: The tribus Pollia was one of the older rural tribes of Rome.

places.title: Vigna Cartoni cistern
places.description: A monumental cistern located in what is now the Caffarella park that was likely once part of the estate of Herodes Atticus.

places.title: Temple of Portunus
places.description: A tetrastyle temple dedicated to the god Portunus and dating to the late second century or early first century BC.

locations.title: OSM location of Temple of Portunus

places.title: Porta Ardeatina
places.description: The Porta Ardeatina was a gate in the city walls of Rome. While it is presumed that the Via Ardeatina exited the walls at this point, debates remain over the nature of the gate; the possibility that it was a postern has been raised.

places.title: Excubitorium
names: excubitorium della VII coorte, Excubitorium della VII Coorte dei Vigili, Trastevere
places.description: A barracks of the seventh cohort of the Vigiles, Rome's urban fire brigade, was located in the Transtiberim.

places.title: Via Taranto columbaria
places.description: Two early imperial columbaria were discovered in 1932 along the Via Taranto.

locations.title: OSM location of Colombari di via Taranto

places.title: Forum Romanum
places.description: The ancient Roman forum.

places.title: Porta Flumentana
places.description: The "Porta Flumentana" or "river gate" was a gate in the Republican-period fortifications along the Tiber River. It is now unlocated. While it may have been in the vicinity of the Pons Aemilius, much debate surrounds its topography.

places.title: Sep. Bibuli
places.description: The tomb of C. Publicius Bibulus, a plebeian aedile, located at Rome at the foot of the Capitoline Hill. It most likely dates to the close of the Republican period.

locations.title: OSM location of Sepolcro di Gaio Poplicio Bibulo

places.title: Semo Sancus, Aedes
places.description: A sanctuary on the Quirinal Hill in Rome sacred to the cult of Semo Sancus Dius Fidius, a cult of Sabine origin said to have been introduced to Rome by Titus Tatius. The dedication of the temple is generally attributed to Sp. Postumius on 5 June 466 BCE.

locations.title: OSM location of Chiesa di San Silvestro al Quirinale

places.title: Porta Ostiensis
places.description: The Porta Ostiensis, now known as the Porta San Paolo, is a gate in Rome's Aurelian Wall from which the Via Ostiensis issues.

places.title: Temple of Quirinus
places.description: The Temple of Quirinus was located near the Capitolium Vetus. The temple was built ex manubiis by Lucius Papirius Cursor in 293 B.C., fulfilling the vow made by his father in 325 B.C. Tradition holds that the republican-period temple was sited on an even earlier altar dedicated by the Sabines. The t

places.title: Horrea Piperataria
places.description: A portion of a warehouse complex dating to the Flavian period, the Horrea Piperataria, was likely destroyed in the fire of 192 CE. Its remains were later incorporated into the substructions of the Basilica Nova (a.k.a. Basilica of Maxentius).

places.title: Colossus Neronis
places.description: The "Colossus Neronis" or "Colossal Statue of Nero" was a monumental bronze statue of the first-century CE emperor reportedly created by Zenodorus. The statue was originally an element of the sprawling Domus Aurea of Nero but the monument endured long after Nero's reign. The statue's original positi

locations.title: OSM location of pedestal of colossus of Nero

places.title: Sororium Tigillum
places.description: Sororium Tigillum describes a wooden beam that stretched across a branch of the Sacra Via that climbed the Oppian Hill near the Compitum Acilii. The monument was flanked by altars of Iuno Sororia and Iuno Curiatius. It is an ancient monument about which there are many stories, the primary one being

places.title: Aurelian Walls
places.description: The Aurelian Walls of Rome began as a fortification system built by Aurelian and Probus between 271 and 275. They enclose an area of approximately 1,400 hectares.

places.title: tribus Ramnes
places.description: The name of a Roman tribe dating from the earliest period of Roman history.

places.title: Amphitheatrum Castrense
places.description: The Amphitheatrum Castrense is a Roman amphitheater built in the third century AD. Its structure was later incorporated into the Aurelianic Walls. Adjacent to the amphitheater is the Christian church of Santa Croce in Gerusalemme.

places.title: Temple of Minerva Medica
places.description: The so-called Temple of Minerva Medica is, in fact, a nymphaeum located along the line of the Anio Vetus aqueduct; it most likely dates to the fourth century AD.

locations.title: OSM location of Tempio di Minerva Medica

places.title: Theatrum Pompei
places.description: Rome's first permanent theater, located in the Campus Martius. The complex was completed under the second consulship of Pompeius Magnus in 55 B.C.

locations.title: OSM location of  Via di Grotta Pinta

places.title: Basilica Porcia
places.description: The Basilica Porcia is considered the first named civil basilica in Rome. The elder Cato is responsible for its construction in 184 BCE. It seems to have been a small structure that took the place of several earlier private atria located between the Clivus Argentarius and the Curia Hostilia. The Bas

places.title: Porta Mugonia
places.description: The Porta Mugonia was one of the three gates of the original Palatine city of Rome (often referred to as "Roma quadrata"). Its precise location can no longer be established and it remains a hotly debated issue for topographers.

places.title: Regia
places.description: The Regia is an ancient complex along the Sacra Via in Rome at the margin of the Forum Romanum, adjacent to the Temple of Vesta. It is understood as a sort of ritual headquarters of Rome's early kings and, later, as a structure connected with the office of the pontifex maximus.

places.title: Thermae Helenianae
places.description: The Thermae Helenianae or Thermae Helenae was a thermal complex located in the Horti Spei Veteris, also referred to as the Horti Variani. The baths were situated near the arcus Neroniani adjacent to the Amphitheatrum Castrense. As Helena, mother of Constantine I, restored them following a fire in 32

places.title: Domus Flavia
places.description: The Domus Flavia is a modern appellation that refers to the palace complex built by the emperor Domitian on the Palatine Hill in Rome. The complex was completed ca. 92 CE. The Flavian complex is considered a part of the larger entity known as Domus Palatina.

places.title: Lupercal
places.description: A cave located at the foot of the Palatine Hill in Rome in which the she-wolf was said to have been found suckling the twins, Romulus and Remus.

places.title: Claudia
places.description: A Roman rural tribe that was one of the most ancient of Rome's gentes. The gens Claudia traced its history to the earliest days of the Roman Republic. Appius Claudius Sabinus Regillensis, in 495 B.C., was the first of its members to hold the consulship.

places.title: So-called Tempio di Venere e Cupido
names: So-called Tempio di Venere e Cupido
places.description: The so-called Temple of Venus and Cupid at Rome is part of the complex of buildings associated with the Sessorian palace. The structure's modern assignation is owed to the discovery of a fragmentary statue of Sallustia Orbiana in the guise of Venus Felix. Sallustia Orbiana was the wife of Alexander

locations.title: OSM location of Tempio di Venere e Cupido

places.title: Via Triumphalis necropolis
places.description: A segment of an imperial necropolis preserved along a portion of a consular road on the Vatican Hill. The Via Triumphalis necropolis was uncovered during the construction of a parking structure in the Via del Pellegrino.

locations.title: OSM location of Necropoli della Via Triumphalis

places.title: Shrine of Strenia
places.description: The Shrine of Strenia was located in the valley of the Colosseum and is mentioned as the starting point of the Sacra Via.

places.title: Schola Praeconum
places.description: The so-called Schola Praeconum is located at the foot of the Palatine Hill near the church of S. Anastasia. A black-and-white floor mosaic discovered during excavations depicts public heralds known as praecones, thus the name of the site.

locations.title: OSM location of Schola Praeconum (Scuola degli Araldi)

places.title: Temple D
places.description: The temple referred to as "Temple D" in the Largo Argentina is likely the Aedes Lares Permarini, sacred to the lares who protect sailors. The largest of the temples in this sacred area, "Temple D" dates to the second century B.C. and remains largely unexcavated.

places.title: Ludus Magnus
places.description: A gladiatorial training school adjacent to the Flavian Amphitheater in Rome. The structure is attested on the Severan marble plan of Rome.

places.title: Ager Romanus
places.description: The rural hinterland of the ancient city of Rome.

places.title: balneum Caesaris
places.description: A bath complex known from the Severan marble plan and perhaps also referred to in the Historia Augusta.

places.title: House of Aufidia Cornelia Valentinilla
places.description: Archaeological excavations in the area of the Aqua Marcia and the Basilica of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem (Rome) in 1887 and 1888 uncovered the remains of lead water pipes identifying this domus as that of one Aufidia Cornelia Valentinilla.

locations.title: OSM location of Domus di Aufidia Cornelia

places.title: Basilica of Santa Pudenziana
places.description: A palaeochristian church dedicated to St. Pudentiana located in Rome and, perhaps, the earliest site of Christian worship in the city. The church is located along the Via Urbana, which follows the course of the ancient vicus Patricius.

places.title: Basilica Ulpia
places.description: The Basilica Ulpia is located in the Forum of Trajan at Rome and derives its name from the emperor Trajan's gentilician nomenclature. The basilica was considered a marvel of ancient Roman architecture by observers, including the historian Ammianus Marcellinus.

places.title: Porticus Boni Eventus
places.description: A portico built in 374 CE by an urban prefect named Claudius near the temple of the god Bonus Eventus.

places.title: Temple B
places.description: A temple vowed by Q. Lutatius Catulus at the battle of Vercellae (30 June, 101 B.C.). The sanctuary is a tholos-type temple and was sometimes referred to as 'aedes Catuli'.

places.title: tribus Tities
places.description: An early Roman tribal division said to date from the time of Romulus.

places.title: templum divi Claudii
places.description: A temple dedicated to the emperor Claudius who was declared divus (deified) after his death in 54 CE. The platform temple occupied a large area of the Caelian Hill in Rome. The construction project was ultimately completed by the Flavians.

locations.title: Imagery location of Temple of Claudius

places.title: Aequimelium
places.description: The Aequimelium was an open area on the southeast slope of the Capitoline Hill. This space may have once been the site of the house of one Spurius Maelius, a Roman citizen of the fifth century BCE who was slain for the crime of wanting to be a king (adfectatio regni).

places.title: Porta Appia
places.description: A gate in the Aurelian Wall through which the Via Appia passed. Now known as Porta S. Sebastiano.

places.title: Temple of Hadrian
places.description: The Temple of Hadrian at Rome, also referred to as the Hadrianeum, was a temple located in the Campus Martius dedicated to the deified Hadrian by Antoninus Pius in 145 CE. Some of the temple's substantial remains were incorporated into a 17th-century building designed by architect Carlo Fontana in R

locations.title: OSM location of Temple of Hadrian

places.title: Clivus Victoriae
places.description: The Clivus Victoriae was a steep street located at or near the southwest corner of the Palatine Hill in Rome.

places.title: Shrine of Venus Cloacina
places.description: The Sacrum Cloacina was a small shrine dedicated to Venus Cloacina, patron divinity of the sewer, and was located near the Tabernae novae in the Forum Romanum. The foundation of the sacellum is extant while images of its likely elevation are found on Roman coins.

locations.title: OSM location of Sacello di Venere Cloacina

places.title: Esquilinus Mons
places.description: The Esquiline Hill is one of the seven hills of Rome. The eastern section of the hill lay outside the Servian Wall, and served as a pauper's cemetery during the archaic and Republican periods.

places.title: Temple of Concord
places.description: The Temple of Concord at Rome was located at the western margin of the Forum Romanum. Its origins are sometimes linked to a vow made by Marcus Furius Camillus in 367 BCE, but the vow may not have been fulfilled until 218 BCE under Lucius Manlius. The sanctuary was rebuilt in 121 BCE and again in 10

locations.title: OSM location of Tempio della Concordia

places.title: Caelius Mons
places.description: The Caelian Hill in Rome.

places.title: Porta Maggiore
places.description: The Porta Maggiore is the ancient Porta Praenestina, an early Imperial gate preserved in the later third century walls built by Aurelian.

places.title: Murus Romuli
places.description: "Murus Romuli" refers to a fortification wall alleged to have surrounded the Palatine Hill in Rome, Italy. Legendary tradition claims it was built by the founder-hero Romulus during the eighth century BCE. The historicity of the wall remains hotly debated.

places.title: Mars, Aedes
places.description: A temple sacred to Mars located on the Via Appia. The shrine was located between the first and second milestones and was dedicated in the fourth century BC. According to Livy, Titus Quinctius dedicated the temple on 1 June 387 BC.

places.title: Septizonium
places.description: The Septizonium (or Septizodium) is a monument located at the extreme southeastern corner of the Palatine Hill, built by the Severan emperors. It is attested to textually in the Historia Augusta; its footprint is visible on the Severan marble plan (Forma Urbis Romae), and its foundations have been e

places.title: Lacus Iuturnae
places.description: The Lacus Iuturnae was a pool built near a spring sacred to Iuturna. Legend held that the Dioscuri watered their horses there after the Battle of Lake Regillus in 495 BCE.

places.title: Baths of Pozzo Pantaleo
places.description: A public bath (thermae) of the Roman Imperial period.

places.title: Pozzo Pantaleo
places.description: The 'Pozzo Pantaleo' is a Roman mausoleum that re-used a cistern of the early Imperial period. In a third phase, the site was repurposed as a shrine dedicated to the Christian Saint Pantaleon.

places.title: Basilica Hilariana
places.description: A basilica erected on the Caelian Hill in Rome under the patronage of Manius Publicus Hilarus and connected to the cult of Cybele and Attis.

places.title: Via Statilia tombs
places.description: Late Republican chamber tombs (ca. 100 B.C.) located at the intersection of the modern Via Statilia and Via di Santa Croce in Rome.

locations.title: OSM location of so-called "Sepolcri repubblicani di Via Statilia"

places.title: Santa Sabina
places.description: A Christian basilica on the Aventine Hill in Rome was founded in the fourth century A.D. The church takes its name from a Christian martyr who was said to have lived on the Aventine. The church is the oldest extant Roman basilica structure that preserves its original plan in the city of Rome.

locations.title: OSM location of Basilica di Santa Sabina all'Aventino

places.title: Porta Aurelia
places.description: A gate in the Aurelian Wall at the summit of the Ianiculum through which the Via Aurelia passes.

locations.title: OSM location of Porta San Pancrazio

places.title: Apollo, Aedes
places.description: The likely site of the original sanctuary to Apollo at Rome. The visible remains belong to the Augustan phase.

places.title: tribus Camilia
places.description: The tribus Camilia is one of the sixteen oldest rural tribes of Rome.

places.title: Viminal Hill
places.description: The Viminal Hill, located between the Quirinal and Esquiline hills, is the smallest of the so-called seven hills of Rome.

places.title: Tullianum
places.description: Prison located at the foot of the Capitoline Hill, named either for Servius Tullius (578–535 BCE) or for the spring (tullus) on which it was constructed. Also known as the Mamertine Prison. The church of San Giuseppe dei Falegnami was constructed on the site in the 11th century CE.

places.title: Crypta Balbi
places.description: The Crypta Balbi, mentioned by name only in the Regionary Catalogues, most likely refers to a vaulted passageway built in the Campus Martius by the proconsul Lucius Cornelius Balbus in 15 BC, who also dedicated a theater there in the same year.

places.title: Porta Salaria
places.description: A gate of the Aurelian Walls of Rome (ca. 271-275 CE) by means of which the Via Salaria exited the city, heading northward. The date was damaged during the bombardment of Rome in 1870 and was subsequently replaced (1873). The replacement gate was demolished in 1921. The site of the Porta Salaria is

places.title: Mira Lanza
places.description: The remains of an Archaic period structure at Mira Lanza, located in Via Luigi Pierantoni.

locations.title: OSM location of Necropoli di Via Pierantoni

places.title: Column of Trajan
places.description: The Column of Trajan (or Trajan's Column) is a victory column that was erected in the Forum of Trajan at Rome ca. 113 in order to commemorate Trajan's victories in the Dacian Wars. The column is particularly noted for its helical historiated bas relief frieze decoration.

places.title: Domus Augustana
places.description: Domus Augustana, a topographic appellation for the central block of the Flavian palace complex on the Palatine Hill attributed to the emperor Domitian.

places.title: Atrium Vestae
places.description: The Atrium Vestae or House of the Vestals refers to an architectural complex on the northwest slope of the Palatine Hill.

locations.title: OSM location of House of the Vestal Virgins

places.title: Rostra
places.description: A large platform erected in the Forum Romanum for senators to deliver orations to a crowd.

places.title: Porta Maggiore Basilica
places.description: The so-called underground basilica near Rome's Porta Maggiore is situated 12 meters below ground level. This vaulted space with a triple nave design is decorated with an elaborate stucco work program. The "basilica" was discovered accidentally in 1917. The site has been dated to the first century BC

locations.title: OSM location of Basilica Sotterranea di Porta Maggiore

places.title: Domus Aventino
places.description: The so-called "Domus Aventino" is located near the Piazza Albania on the Aventine Hill in Rome. This archaeological site was identified in 2014 and preserves multiple phases of human activity, including elements of Rome's archaic fortifications and the remains of a well-appointed domus.

places.title: Chalcidicum
places.description: Augustus uses the generic term Chalcidicum to describe a porch he built as an approach to the Curia Iulia.

places.title: Ara Pacis Augustae
places.description: The "Altar of Augustan Peace" was located in the Campus Martius of Rome. It was originally situated to the west of the Via Lata, near the eastern end of Augustus' Horologium. The reconstructed fragments of the altar are now housed in a museum located on the Tiber's banks in the Piazza Augusto Impera

locations.title: Imagery Location: Original position of the Ara Pacis

places.title: Casa dei Grifi
places.description: A late Republican domus of the Palatine Hill that was later consumed by the substructures of the Domitianic wing of the Flavian palace. The Casa dei Grifi preserves important wall paintings that are transitional from the First to the Second Pompeian style. Giacomo Boni discovered the domus in 1912.

locations.title: OSM location of Casa dei Grifi

places.title: Temple A
places.description: So-called "Temple A" is a structure of the third century B.C. and is likely the Temple of Juturna that was vowed by Caius Lutatius Catulus following his victory against the Carthaginians in 241 B.C. It was later converted into a church, the apse of which remains visible.

places.title: Temple C
places.description: The so-called "Temple C" of the Largo Argentina sacred area may be dedicated to the Italic goddess Feronia.

places.title: Temple of Mars Ultor
places.description: The Temple of Mars Ultor was dedicated in the Forum of Augustus in 2 B.C., fulfilling a vow that Octavian had made to the god in 42 B.C.

locations.title: OSM location: Temple of Mars Ultor

places.title: Temple of Hercules Victor
places.description: A monopteros in the Forum Boarium at Rome built in the late second century BC, perhaps by L. Mummius Achaicus.

locations.title: OSM location: Temple of Hercules Victor

places.title: Sepulcretum
places.description: A modern appellation of the ancient Iron Age necropolis uncovered along the Sacra Via adjacent to the Temple of Antoninus and Faustina in April 1902. Giacomo Boni and others conducted extensive excavations at the site.

places.title: Curia Iulia
places.description: Construction of the Curia Julia was begun by Julius Caesar and completed by Augustus in 29 BCE. It replaced the former senate house, the Curia Hostilia.

places.title: Via Triumphalis
places.description: A road running from the Pons Neronianus toward Monte Mario, eventually joining the Via Clodia some 7 miles from Rome.

places.title: Palatium Sessorianum
places.description: Palatium Sessorianum is of unknown origins. It was situated at the extreme south-east of Region V and it adjoined the amphitheatrum Castrense. It pre-dated the Aurelian wall. The portions of the complex within the line of the walls was an imperial residence by the time of Constantine.

places.title: Horrea Vespasiani
places.description: A warehouse complex on the Palatine slope adjacent to the Sacra Via.

places.title: Mutatorium Caesaris
places.description: An imperial property opposite the Baths of Caracalla that is mentioned in the Regionary Catalogues and also preserved on a fragment of the Severan marble plan.

places.title: Saepta Iulia
places.description: An enclosure in the Campus Martius surrounded by porticoes built by Marcus Agrippa before ca. 26 BCE.

places.title: Auditorium Maecenatis
places.description: An early Imperial building on the Esquiline Hill in Rome, the Auditorium Maecenatis has been connected with Maecenas as it stands in the area of his gardens (horti). While its precise function is unknown, the building may have served as a conservatory.

locations.title: OSM location of Auditorium di Mecenate

places.title: Cloaca Maxima
places.description: The Cloaca Maxima drained the valley of the Forum Romanum. The sewer originates as a canalized drain in the late sixth century BCE. It would eventually be vaulted and interred. It drains into the Tiber River.

locations.title: OSM location of mouth of the Cloaca Maxima

places.title: Porta Latina
places.description: A city gate in the Aurelian Wall that was substantially modified under Honorius in the fifth century A.D.

places.title: Temple of Jupiter Optimus Maximus
names: Temple of Jupiter Optimus Maximus Capitolinus
places.description: The chief temple of the city of Rome was located on the Capitoline Hill.

locations.title: GeoHack location of Temple of Jupiter Optimus Maximus

places.title: San Nicola in Carcere
places.description: San Nicola in Carcere is a titular church in Rome's historical district (rione) Sant'Angelo, close to the Forum Boarium. The twelfth-century church is built atop the remains of Roman temples of the ancient Forum Holitorium and incorporates their remains into its structure.

locations.title: OSM location of San Nicola in Carcere

places.title: Hypogeum of Trebius Giustus
places.description: A tomb of the fourth century A.D. located on the Via Latina.

locations.title: OSM location of Ipogeo di Trebio Giusto

places.title: Vicus Iugarius
places.description: An ancient street that led from the Forum Romanum to the porta Carmentalis, passing between the basilica Iulia and the temple of the Castors.

places.title: Vicus Censorius
places.description: A street located on the Tiber Island that connected the Pons Cestius and Pons Fabricius. It is cited on the so-called "Capitoline Base".

places.title: Temple of Venus Genetrix
names: Tempio di Venere Genitrice al Foro di Cesare
places.description: The Temple of Venus Genetrix located in the Forum Iulium was dedicated ca. 46 BCE.

locations.title: OSM location: Temple of Venus Genetrix

places.title: House of Livia
places.description: The so-called "House of Livia" on the Palatine Hill in Rome is a multi-phase domus with both Republican and Imperial phases.

locations.title: OSM location of Casa di Livia

places.title: Basilica Opimia
places.description: A civil basilica built in the Forum Romanum ca. 121 BCE by Lucius Opimius. This basilica was likely razed in 7 BCE.

places.title: Athenaeum of Hadrian (Rome)
places.description: The Athenaeum of Hadrian was located in regio VII near the Capitoline Hill in Rome. Founded by the Emperor Hadrian, it was designated for the promotion of literary and scientific studies and named after the city of Athens. Excavations connected to the Metro C line revealed a complex in the vicinity

locations.title: Imagery location of the Athenaeum of Hadrian
OSM location of Auditorium of Hadrian

places.title: Castra Peregrina
places.description: Located on the Caelian Hill, the Castra Peregrina housed Roman soldiers.

places.title: Tarpeian Rock
places.description: The Tarpeian Rock (Tarpeius mons) is a steep rocky cliff on the south side of the Capitoline Hill in Rome. Certain adjudicated criminals were tossed from the Tarpeian Rock to their deaths in antiquity. According to Varro, Tarpeius mons may be the earliest name of the Capitoline Hill.

places.title: Emporium
places.description: The river port of the ancient city of Rome that was located between the Aventine Hill and the Rione Testaccio, formally established perhaps in 193 BCE.

places.title: Vicus Drusianus
places.description: A street located in Regio I of ancient Rome that is known from the so-called Capitoline Base (CIL 6, 975). Part of its course may correspond to the Via della Ferratella in Laterano.

locations.title: OSM location of Via della Ferratella in Laterano

places.title: Column of Marcus Aurelius
names: columna centenaria divorum Marci et Faustinae
places.description: The Column of Marcus Aurelius is a monumental victory column erected along the Via Lata between 176 and 193 CE. The monument celebrated victories realized against the Marcomanni and the Sarmatians (172-175 CE).

locations.title: OSM location of Column of Marcus Aurelius

places.title: Porta Asinaria
places.description: The Porta Asinaria is a gate of the Aurelian Walls on the Caelian Hill, located immediately southwest of the Porta S. Giovanni.

places.title: Circus Maximus Mithraeum
places.description: A mithraeum adjacent to the Circus Maximus and facing the carceres of the same was located at the margin of the Forum Boarium and now situated beneath a building in the via dell'Ara Massima. The site was excavated in 1931.

locations.title: Imagery location of Mitreo del Circo Massimo

places.title: Palatinus Mons
places.description: The central hill of Rome, Italy. Legend held that Romulus founded the city of Rome on the Palatine Hill following an augural contest with Remus, his brother.

places.title: Vatican necropolis
places.description: The Vatican necropolis lies beneath Vatican City, specifically beneath the present St. Peter's Basilica, at depths ranging from 5 to 12 meters. The necropolis was partially exposed by means of archaeological excavations in 1940-1949. The necropolis was an open-air burial ground that included both ma

places.title: Lucus Stimulae
places.description: A grove sacred to Stimula, located at the southwestern foot of the Aventine Hill.

places.title: Volcanal
places.description: The Volcanal was an open-air sanctuary of Vulcan located in the valley of the Forum Romanum on the slopes of the Capitoline Hill. The earliest phases of the sanctuary likely predate the forum itself.

places.title: Forum of Nerva
places.description: A forum complex at Rome begun under Domitian but completed under Nerva and dedicated in A.D. 97. Sometimes referred to as the Forum Transitorium, the complex was the next to last of the imperial fora at Rome.

locations.title: OSM location of Forum of Nerva

places.title: Horologium Augusti
places.description: The Horologium Augusti or Solarium Augusti was an ancient monument of the Campus Martius built during the reign of Augustus. In theory, it functioned as a giant solar marker. An obelisk relocated to Rome from Heliopolis served as the gnomon. The obelisk today stands in the Piazza di Monte Citorio.

locations.title: OSM location of Piazza di San Lorenzo in Lucina

places.title: tribus Galeria
places.description: The tribus Galeria was one of the older rural tribes of ancient Rome

places.title: Porta Collina
places.description: A gate in Rome's Servian Wall located on the Quirinal Hill.

places.title: Murus Terreus Carinarum
places.description: An early earthwork at Rome described by Varro, the Murus Terreus may have been part of the so-called Servian Wall. It was likely located on the Oppian Hill, between the Subura and the Carinae.

places.title: Sep. Scipionum
places.description: A family tomb of the Cornelii Scipiones near the Porta San Sebastiano in use from the third century B.C. to the first century A.D.

locations.title: Imagery location of the Sep. Scipionum
OSM location of Sepolcro degli Scipioni
